assets.label: Contact shadow â€” soft ground occlusion blob
assets.notes: AMBIENT OCCLUSION, NOT A CAST SHADOW. Non-directional on purpose: it is the darkening where an object occludes ambient light at its base, so it is correct at every time of day and does NOT need redoing when a sun direction is chosen. Raheem, 2026-08-07, worried a shadow would have to change once time-of-day is picked â€” this one will not. Cast shadows are a separate, later, directional asset. Reusable under any building or prop; scale to the object's width.

assets.label: Tan kerb (plain, darker) â€” wang 32
assets.notes: Raheem, 2026-08-07: the tan+white brick should be the ROAD; the kerb should be 'a solid or darker tan block, not white and tan spotted'. So this is the same brick with the cream speckle removed (543 px above luma 195 mapped to base tan rgb(197,150,106)) and darkened to 0.70 â€” mortar only to 0.90, else the kerb becomes a black grid. Road/kerb luma gap 153 -> 104 = 49. Zero generations. A grey-stone recolour was tried first and rejected: 'I actually like the colour of the tan bricks.'

assets.label: The Forge â€” exterior, PixelLab redraw (v2)
assets.notes: THE QUALITY FIX. v1 was Gemini art box-downsampled: measured 0.6% flatness and 26,393 colours â€” a photo shrunk down, not pixel art, which is why it read soft beside the kit. v2 feeds the ORIGINAL 942px Gemini crop to PixelLab POST /image-to-pixelart (first ever use of that endpoint in this project; 1 generation) which REDRAWS it. Then: white keyed by border flood, ground cut at row 187 (ground share jumped 16%->60%), fabric quantized to 40 colours, and the portal given its OWN 24-colour ramp so the rainbow is not starved by the stone. Result 64 colours, 42.9% flatness, saturation 58.4. Castle wall reference is 48 colours / 59.4%.

assets.label: The Forge â€” portal glow, separate layer
assets.notes: The doorway vortex on its own layer so it can be lit independently during the walk-into-the-forge transition, and so it does not compete with the stone for palette slots. Ellipse centre (143,160) r 27x24 in the 320x200 redraw.

assets.label: The Archivist â€” exterior, PixelLab redraw (v2)
assets.notes: Same pipeline as castle.forge.v2. Original 941px Gemini crop -> POST /image-to-pixelart (1 gen, $0.0100) -> white keyed by border flood -> ground cut at row 264 (ground share 42%->64%) -> quantized to 48 colours -> dehalo. NO protected glow region here, unlike the forge: 46.5% of this building is above saturation 60 because the blue stone and teal dome ARE the building, so a saturation split would have bucketed half the facade as glow. Straight quantize 48 measured better anyway: flatness 37.4%->64.7%, 48 colours, only -7% saturation. Castle wall reference is 48 colours / 59.4% flatness.

assets.label: Curtain wall, straight run â€” v3 (16-bit topdown kit)
assets.notes: 318x212, 38 colours, 72.6% flatness (kit baseline 59.4%). Front and back runs; mirror vertically for the opposite side. Tiles horizontally. Keys to 0px on purpose â€” it runs to the frame edge and has no surround to remove. Leonardo/Gemini plate (Raheem, improved from a cut reference) -> lib/harmonise_materials.py (metal pass, then stone COLOUR-CAST pass; value never scaled) -> POST /image-to-pixelart -> harmonise again, anchored on the wall, because PixelLab reinterprets colour hard (stone hue ran 232deg on the wall to 170deg on the battle tower) -> lib/quantize_shared.py, ONE 48-colour palette across all five with equal per-piece sampling -> lib/key_white.py -> dehalo --min-value 185. Reproduce with scripts/bg-harness/castle-pixellab.sh.

assets.label: Curtain wall, side run â€” v3 (16-bit topdown kit)
assets.notes: 125x318, 24 colours, 68.6% flatness. Left and right runs; mirror horizontally for the opposite side. Shows NO face band, which is correct: at this camera tilt a north-south wall is nearly edge-on, so only the walkway is visible. Its source plate had the crenel pattern destroyed across rows 400-650 (railing quality 0.5-1.9 against ~3.5 elsewhere); repaired by cloning rows 652-902, a whole pattern offset away. assets.label: Gatehouse â€” v3 (16-bit topdown kit)
assets.sourceSubject: gemini G5 'remove the centre crystal' plate

Floating runes were removed from the source plate: the solid cores came off as their own connected components, the palest glyphs had to be cleared by region because they sit above the white cutoff and nothing could see them. assets.label: Corner tower â€” v3 (16-bit topdown kit)
assets.sourceSubject: composited from the battle tower plate, zero generations
assets.notes: 183x269, 46 colours, 58.9% flatness. Terminates a wall run and turns a corner â€” put one on every corner and the kit needs no corner wall piece at all, which is how both reference tilemaps do it. Built by grafting the battle tower's crown (rows 0-172) onto its own base (rows 400-end), skipping the middle storeys: same plate, so palette, angle and lighting match by construction. Seam lands on a cornice; widths there are 200 and 205. SCALE IS NOT 1:1 WITH THE WALLS. This piece's plate was framed at a different internal scale in Leonardo; composited against the wall, its door only matches the wall's doors at about 2.6x. That multiplier is already baked into this asset (generated at scale 0.8125 vs the walls' 0.3125), so place it at the same Phaser scale as the walls. assets.label: Battle Tower â€” v3 (16-bit topdown kit)
assets.notes: 184x457, 47 colours, 54.8% flatness. The landmark that rises over the back wall â€” game function, not decoration: CLAUDE.md makes the tower the game's gate. Cut out of a full landscape by keying grass and taking the seed's island; the banner poles reach up and touch the curtain-wall arch, so they were severed above the crown rim rather than clipped (a box low enough to cut the wall also slices the crown). Banners are deliberately absent â€” a flag should ripple, so it belongs in a Phaser layer, not baked into a static plate. Cliff kit v1 — floor
assets.sourceSubject: pixellab create-tiles-pro building kit (cliff), tile_id db40f575
assets.notes: PixelLab /create-tiles-pro, tile_feature=building, building_wall_tiles=3, square_topdown, high top-down, tile_size 32, seed 7. 20 generations. A cliff is structurally a building kit: a plateau floor, connectable 3-tile walls and every corner. /create-tileset cannot do it — it returns a FLAT 16-tile boundary between two ground materials with no vertical face. Tiles are 52x111 for a 32px cell, so they OVERLAP and are placed on a 32px grid as images rather than painted as tilemap tiles. tile_feature blocks style_images, so there is no Leonardo design step here — colour comes from the shared castle-kit palette instead. Kit B of two; kit A was the accidental duplicate and is not shipped. See _rules.json for the placement map.
